introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Philosophy 2 (0790), Paper 2 (Philosophical Writing and Analysis), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: three hours.**

Candidates are required to answer FOUR questions, choosing at least one question from each section.

Each essay question shall be marked according to the following criteria:
- Coherence and organization of material;
- Clear presentation of the problematic;
- Identification and development of the Thesis, Antithesis, Synthesis and Conclusion as prescribed.

Each question carries 25 marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde dit « Candidates are required to answer FOUR questions, choosing at least one question from each section » (quatre questions au total, au moins une par section ; trois sections de deux questions : Section One 1-2, Section Two 3-4, Section Three 5-6). `regles_choix` porte le minimum, une règle `parmi 1 sur 2` par section ; la règle « 4 questions en tout » n'est pas exprimable en entier et est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : chaque question est imprimee « 25 marks » (4 x 25 = 100). Les questions de textes (5 et 6) ont leurs points par sous-question : Q5 = 5 + (2 x 2) + 3 + 4 + 4 + 5 = 25 ; Q6 = 5 + (2 x 2) + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 25. Aucun écart de somme constaté, aucun point corrigé. La page de garde de 2024 ne donne pas de barème par partie pour les dissertations (contrairement à 2022) : les titres « (5 marks) », « (7 marks) »... des corrigés de dissertation ne sont donc pas utilisés, seule la structure exigée (problématique, thèse, antithèse, synthèse, conclusion) est suivie.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans accès à une source. Les auteurs et positions cités sont ceux de l'histoire de la philosophie établie, sans citation littérale, sans numéro de page et sans date ; à faire relire par un enseignant de philosophie avant mise en avant.

Sujet scanné (3 pages) avec filigrane gcerevision.com / Kawlo sans incidence sur la lecture ; aucune figure. Page de garde vérifiée : ADVANCED LEVEL, Philosophy 2, Paper 2 (Philosophical Writing and Analysis), code 0790, JUNE 2024, trois heures.

Q3 : le sujet dit « The ethno-philosophical trend represents an authentic approach to African philosophy. Do you agree? ». Attributions classiques (Tempels, Mbiti, Kagame, Hountondji, Towa, Eboussi Boulaga, Wiredu, Oruka, Gyekye, Senghor) données dans leurs grandes lignes, sans citation, sans titre exact d'ouvrage hormis « African Philosophy: Myth and Reality » (Hountondji), sans date. Mention de Hegel et de Lévy-Bruhl comme cibles des critiques africaines : lecture usuelle.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The ethno-philosophical trend represents an authentic approach to African philosophy. Do you agree?

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction and problematic.** African philosophy as a discipline began with a debate about its own existence and nature: is there an African philosophy, and what does it consist of? Ethno-philosophy is the trend which holds that African philosophy is the collective worldview of African peoples, found in their myths, proverbs, languages, rites and customs, and which the philosopher describes and systematises. The problem is whether this trend gives an *authentic* approach to African philosophy, that is, one that is truly African and truly philosophical.

**Thesis: ethno-philosophy is an authentic approach.**
- *It starts from the African's own world.* Placide Tempels, in his work on Bantu philosophy, argued that the Bantu have a coherent ontology based on the notion of vital force, and that it can be reconstructed from their behaviour and language. John Mbiti studied African religions and notions of time and community, and Alexis Kagame analysed the Kinyarwanda language to find categories of Bantu-Rwandan thought. For these authors, philosophy is not only a Western invention: every people has a worldview that answers questions about being, the person, God and society.
- *It restores the dignity of Africans.* Against colonial and Western claims (Hegel, Lévy-Bruhl) that Africans are "pre-logical" or without history and thought, ethno-philosophy shows that African societies have a rich system of thought. In the movement of Negritude, Senghor stressed the African way of knowing by emotion and participation, as a value.
- *It preserves a heritage.* The oral traditions, proverbs and myths are the memory of the continent; to collect and interpret them is to keep alive what colonisation tried to destroy, and gives a base for identity and for development.
- *It matches a broad conception of philosophy,* as a reflection of a people on its own experience, and not only an academic argument.

**Antithesis: ethno-philosophy is not authentic, or not philosophy.**
- *Paulin Hountondji* (African Philosophy: Myth and Reality) criticised it as "ethnophilosophy": it treats philosophy as a collective, unconscious, unanimous system, a "unanimism" which ignores the individual thinkers, disagreement and debate that mark real philosophy. He added that the first ethno-philosophers (like Tempels) were Europeans writing for Europeans, so that the approach reflects a Western curiosity more than an African one. A set of beliefs is material for ethnology, not yet philosophy, which needs critical, argued, reflective discourse.
- *Marcien Towa and Fabien Eboussi Boulaga* also criticised it as nostalgic and as locking Africans in the past; philosophy must face the problems of present Africa (domination, underdevelopment), and philosophy cannot be reduced to the preservation of tradition.
- *Kwasi Wiredu* asked for a critical examination of tradition and "conceptual decolonisation", separating what is rational from what is mere custom or superstition. *Henry Odera Oruka* showed with "sage philosophy" that there are individual African sages who reason critically within traditional societies; so philosophy is not only collective.
- *Practical risk:* the idea of a single African worldview ignores the diversity of the continent and can serve to justify any tradition, including oppressive ones.

**Synthesis.** Ethno-philosophy is authentic in its starting point, because it recognises that African cultures contain philosophical material and gives Africans back their own voice, but it is not sufficient: the material has to be analysed, argued and criticised by individual thinkers, as Hountondji, Wiredu and Gyekye (who proposes a critical reconstruction of tradition) demand. It is therefore a stage, or a source, and not the whole of African philosophy.

**Conclusion.** I agree only partly. Ethno-philosophy is an authentic approach in that it rests on African thought and answers the colonial denial of African reason, but it is not the only authentic approach, nor the most rigorous. An authentic African philosophy combines the study of the people's heritage with critical, personal and contemporary reflection.
